findings.text: Each header defines a single inclusion guard macro that marks the header as already processed.

Late PCIe2 core register group spans nine slots from 0x0F14 through 0x0F38 with a gap at 0x0F2C, assigning in ascending order reset status, link-down reset enable, misc interrupt enable, transmit debug config, misc config, misc status, then interrupt enable, clear and status.

Mailbox and power registers place interrupt status, mask and backplane mailbox at low offsets 0x090, 0x094 and 0x098, reference-up timing at 0x1814, device status control 2 at config offset 0xD4 with link-training enable bit 0x400, and power-management clock period at 0x184C.
PCIe2 driver private record holds a pointer to its parent backplane core followed by a 16-bit requested transfer size.
Six small accessors forward 16-bit and 32-bit reads, writes, bit-set and masked clear operations to the parent core helpers using the stored core pointer plus caller offset and value.

Clock management register lives at 0x01E0. Force and request bits occupy 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08 and 0x10, with hardware off at 0x20 and high-quality demand at 0x40. External requests use mask 0x0700 shifted by 8. Availability appears at 0x010000 and 0x020000, current-clock indicators at 0x040000 and 0x080000, and external status uses mask 0x07000000 shifted by 24.
On 4328 stepping A0 the two availability bits are swapped, so high-throughput availability is reported at 0x010000 and low-power availability at 0x020000.

Out-of-band select sits at 0x0100. IO control at 0x0408 packs clock enable 0x0001, forced gated clock 0x0002, core field 0x3FFC, power-management enable 0x4000 and self-test enable 0x8000. IO status at 0x0500 packs core field 0x0FFF, 64-bit DMA 0x1000, gated clock 0x2000, self-test error 0x4000 and done 0x8000. Reset control and status sit at 0x0800 and 0x0804 with reset asserted by 0x0001. Northstar ROM boot device decodes from mask 0x0003 as NOR 0x0000, NAND 0x0001 or ROM 0x0002.

PCI configuration places power status at 0x44 with power-enable bit 0x100, backplane windows at 0x80 and 0x84, serial PROM control at 0x88 with write enable 0x10, burst control at 0x8C, PCI and backplane interrupt status at 0x90 and 0x98 with mask at 0x94, second window alias at 0xAC, GPIO input output and direction at 0xB0 0xB4 and 0xB8, plus slow-clock radio-disable crystal and PLL bits 0x10 0x20 0x40 and 0x80, and a second-generation PCIe window alias at 0x70.

System-on-chip map fixes SDRAM at zero, host PCI memory and config at 0x08000000 and 0x0C000000 each 64 MB, byte-swapped SDRAM at 0x10000000, region-2 SDRAM at 0x80000000, client DMA windows at 0x40000000 and 0x80000000 each 1 GB, PCIe DMA low half at zero with high halves 0x80000000 and 0xC0000000 for the two controllers, and flash regions at 0x1FC00000 size 4 MB and 0x1C000000 size 32 MB.
Name limits cap operation names at 16 bytes, interpreter names at 32 bytes, and interpreter table size at 100 entries.
Interpreter registration links into a list and stores an open file reference, a user-namespace usage counter, a path pointer and a trailing flexible name field.
Binary-parameter BPF flags assign five distinct low powers of two for preserving argument zero, credential override, exec file descriptor, transparent interpretation and loader indication.
Operation vector pairs a match predicate and a load routine with a fixed-size name buffer sized by the operation-name limit.
In the sampled configuration lookup always reports absence, release and type-test helpers do nothing beyond returning false, indicating a disabled optional feature.
Integrity flags use low bits 0 through 7 for ownership, remap, no-check, IP checksum, user copy and guard, reference-tag and application-tag checks, with bit 15 marking mempool backing.
Integrity payload stores a byte iterator, short counts for used and maximum vectors, short control flags, a 16-bit application tag and a pointer to the vector array.
Guard plus both tag checks form the verification group, and the clone group adds mapped-integrity and IP-checksum to that verification group for propagation across clones.

Presence test returns the attached payload only when the request operation flags ask for integrity, otherwise absence. Flag test is true only when a payload exists and the requested bit is set. Two iterators walk payload vectors and then all chained integrity vectors in order.
Integrity seed is exactly the sector stored in the payload iterator, readable and writable through paired helpers.

When integrity support is compiled out, mapping helpers report invalid argument, unmap, prepare, advance and trim do nothing, clone and page-add report success without action, allocation reports invalid argument through an error pointer, presence always reports absence and flag test always reports false.
Block vector ceiling is 256 entries while the inline vector ceiling tracks the generic IO vector maximum.

Segment cap is the smaller of caller count and vector ceiling. Iterator helpers expose current vector, page, length and offset, while sector helpers convert byte size with a 512-byte shift and add it to the start sector to obtain end position.

Data direction is write only for write operations and read otherwise, operation code is the masked low portion of operation flags, and flag helpers test, set or clear a single numbered bit in the bio flags word.
Data presence requires a non-null bio with non-zero remaining size and excludes discard, secure erase and write-zeroes operations.

The no-advance class is exactly discard, secure erase and write-zeroes. Data address is available only when data is present, otherwise null. Segment stepping advances through the vector count and reports exhaustion at the end.

Page splitting converts one bio vector into page-sized pieces, starting from its page plus offset on first use and then advancing page by page, emitting the smaller of remaining page space and remaining vector length and moving to the next vector when consumed.

Full iterator advance moves the sector forward by whole 512-byte units and, for no-advance operations, only shrinks the remaining size, while normal operations also slide the vector index and offset forward by the same byte count.
Advancing beyond the recorded remaining size triggers a one-time warning, discards the remainder and reports failure instead of walking off the vector table.

Single-step advance assumes progress stays within one vector, rolling the index forward only when offset exactly reaches the current vector length, otherwise updating offset in place while always deducting from remaining size.

Full bio advance completes immediately when consuming the entire remainder and otherwise delegates to a shared helper. Segment and vector iteration forms restart from a saved iterator, yield each current vector while size remains, and step by that vector length.

Segment count is zero for the no-advance class and otherwise equals the number of iterated segments. The last-piece test holds exactly when remaining size equals current vector length. The all-vectors form scans the raw vector array by index.

Reference acquisition marks the bio referenced with an ordering barrier before incrementing its count, while count initialization marks referenced only for non-single counts. Base accessors return the first vector, its page and its folio, warning if called on a cloned bio, with folio derived from the page header.
Folio iteration state holds current folio, byte offset and length for caller use plus private next folio, remaining segment bytes and vector index for resumption.

Folio walk starts each vector by locating its folio and offset and capping length to the smaller of folio remainder and vector remainder, continues within the same vector by stepping to successive folios until exhausted, then resumes at the next vector, terminating with a null folio past the last vector.

Splitting returns the original bio when the requested sector count covers it and otherwise delegates to a split helper. Bioset option bits mark vector need, rescuer need and per-CPU caching. Allocation uses the filesystem bioset. Atomic context is true under RCU read sections with preemption support or more generally when preemption is unavailable or disabled.
